datasets.name: SDFVD (Small-scale Deepfake Forgery Video Dataset)
datasets.structure: zip -> SDFVD.zip -> SDFVD/videos_real/vN.mp4 and SDFVD/videos_fake/vsN.mp4 (nested archive)
datasets.issues: 0 unreadable videos; 53/53 index pairs have both a real (vN) and fake (vsN) clip with identical resolution/frame count -> fakes are derived from the paired reals, so splits MUST keep pairs together. Resolutions: {'1280x720': 52, '378x720': 16, '1280x674': 22, '404x720': 16}
datasets.verdict: Suitable for an EXPERIMENTAL video baseline
datasets.reason: Balanced and labelled, but only 106 clips; every metric has a very wide confidence interval.

datasets.name: DeepfakeTIMIT
datasets.structure: plain TAR (despite the .gz name) -> DeepfakeTIMIT/{higher,lower}_quality/<speaker>/<utt>.avi + .wav ; 32 speakers; extras: {'': 67, '.avi': 640, '.wav': 640, '.txt': 1, '.png': 2, '.mov': 3}
datasets.issues: Contains ONLY face-swapped (fake) videos - no real counterpart (VidTIMIT originals are not included) -> cannot train a real-vs-fake video classifier. WAVs are the unmodified original speech (README), byte-identical in HQ/LQ folders -> genuine human speech only, no synthetic class.
datasets.verdict: Partly suitable (speaker data) / not suitable for deepfake classifier training
datasets.used_for: Module 4 speaker-verification calibration (speaker-disjoint split) and pipeline tests; NOT for Module 1/2 training
datasets.reason: Speaker-labelled clean speech supports an experimental identity-comparison calibration; one-class media cannot train detectors.

datasets.name: UyghurDF preview v0.1
datasets.structure: tar.gz -> bonafide|spoof/<generator>/<split>/*.wav + metadata.csv + protocol.txt; 16 kHz mono 16-bit
datasets.issues: README: listening sample, 'not for detector training or evaluation'. 18 generators, only 3 bona-fide clips. Uyghur language only.
datasets.used_for: Testing audio loading, preprocessing, feature extraction and the audio upload workflow
datasets.reason: Too small and explicitly not intended for training/evaluation; no accuracy is claimed from it.

datasets.name: SMS Spam Collection v.1 (UCI)
datasets.issues: 415 exact duplicate texts (removed before splitting to avoid leakage). English, 2011-era UK/Singapore SMS; 'spam' is mostly promotions, not scams.
datasets.used_for: Module 5 text classifier (TF-IDF); also vocabulary for unknown-case detection
datasets.reason: Labelled, adequately sized; domain shift to emails/job ads/Indian UPI scams is not covered.

datasets.name: Phishing Websites (UCI, ARFF)
datasets.structure: zip -> Training Dataset.arff (31 attributes incl. Result), .old.arff, feature description docx
datasets.issues: Pre-computed categorical features (-1/0/1) such as SSLfinal_State, age_of_domain, Page_Rank that require crawling/WHOIS lookups; URLs themselves are not included, so features cannot be computed for a new message/screenshot.
datasets.verdict: Not suitable for the live app
datasets.reason: Cannot be applied to arbitrary uploaded evidence without web crawling/external lookups, which are out of scope.

datasets.name: 1000 QR Images of Malicious and Benign QR codes (2025)
datasets.structure: zip -> .rar -> benign_qr_images_500/*.png + malicious_qr_images_500/*.png (nested RAR; needs unrar-cffi/unrar/7-Zip)
datasets.issues: 13 images could not be decoded by OpenCV; labels come from folder names; benign URLs are mostly well-known sites, malicious ones throw-away domains (sampling bias).
datasets.verdict: Suitable for QR-decoding tests and an EXPERIMENTAL URL-lexical hint model
datasets.used_for: Module 6 QR decoding test; URL lexical model shown beside URLs (not fused)
datasets.reason: Decoded payloads are URL strings with benign/malicious labels, but the model may learn dataset artefacts.
